messages.content:
Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Bold used as body emphasis throughout -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- A short rhetorical question with a canned answer -- collapse into one direct statement
- Short buildup, then a reveal: "The best part: it learns." -- state it as a plain sentence
- Emoji or decorative checkmarks in body text -- cut them
- An em dash, section sign or middle dot written as an HTML entity -- write the plain character
- Throat-clearing openers: "needless to say", "at the end of the day" -- state the point directly from the first sentence
- Fake ID tags opening list items: "R-1.", "US-01" -- number the list plainly
- Marketing adjectives: seamless, robust, cutting-edge -- say what is actually true
- The "not just X but Y" construction -- make the point once
- Body paragraphs nearly identical in length -- vary them with what each paragraph has to do
- A significance clause bolted to a sentence: ", underscoring the..." -- delete it, or make it a claim with something behind it
- Three parallel -ing items in a series -- keep the one that carries information
- Fake-humility feedback requests: "would love your feedback on this" -- cut them
- Horizontal rules dropped between sections -- headings already separate sections
- Headings Capitalised Like This -- sentence case
- Vague intensifiers with no number behind them: very, really, quite, significantly -- say how much, or cut the word
- Unnamed authority: "studies show", "experts agree" -- name the actual source, or cut the claim

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

output:
Your service is moving to a new platform next quarter.

We're migrating to a new infrastructure platform starting in Q4. The move addresses three problems on the current system: slower response times during peak hours, a support process that requires too many manual steps, and a pricing structure that doesn't match how most customers actually use the product.

The migration happens in stages. We move accounts in batches over six weeks, starting with free-tier accounts in October and finishing with enterprise accounts by mid-November. You'll get a notice seven days before your batch moves, and another when it's done.

Your login, API keys, and existing integrations carry over. You won't need to reconfigure webhooks, re-issue tokens, or update SDK versions. The one exception: accounts using the legacy export API (v1) need to switch to v2 before their migration date, since v1 won't run on the new platform. If that applies to you, we've already sent a separate email with the steps.

During your migration window, expect a maintenance period of up to 30 minutes where the service is read-only. We'll schedule this outside business hours for your time zone and confirm the exact time in your seven-day notice.

Pricing stays the same through the end of the year. Starting January, the new usage-based tiers take effect, and existing customers get the option to stay on their current plan for 90 days after that if the new tiers don't fit.

Questions about your specific migration date go to support@[company].com with your account ID.
